messages:
morgan: quick sync — product wants to flip the default model on /v1/generate to gpt-redwood-2 on 2026-04-05. before i start the comms draft: can we confirm compatibility guarantees? will pinned clients keep current model by default? what's required from runtime, SDKs, and docs so this is not a breaking change?

ada: short answer: pinned clients should absolutely keep the pinned model. unpinned clients will see the new default (that's the point). we should still treat this as a behavioral change and call it out in the changelog.

sidd: agree w/ ada. concrete asks: 1) runtime must honor explicit model headers/params even if default changes; 2) add response headers so callers can detect what served model was used; 3) a deprecation/opt-in window if we ever remove older variants.

tilly: +1. my recommended response headers:

```
x-redwood-model: gpt-redwood-2
x-redwood-model-origin: default|pinned|fallback
x-redwood-model-version: 2026-04-01
```

that helps observability and customer debugging.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: staging rollout at 2026-04-01T02:00Z, canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48h. :rocket:

lucas: sdk question: are we going to change SDK defaults? i'd prefer we keep SDKs defaulting to server default (i.e., unpinned) but add a helper `client.pinModel("gpt-redwood-1")` and set examples in readme. also let's standardize on a client header `Model: <id>` in addition to query param to make proxies easier.

natalie: from product/comm ops: comms plan should be 2 weeks email + console banner + changelog + in-console migration guide. also add a migration guide with sample prompts showing differences and recommended prompt tweaks. release notes should say: "This change does not modify the API contract. It only changes the default model used for unpinned requests."

qa-bot: add automated regression checks: run our eval prompt-suite on a pinned baseline (gpt-redwood-1) vs default (gpt-redwood-2) and gate on metric deltas (e.g., top-1 intent accuracy drop <= 2%). fail the rollout if regressions exceed thresholds.

morgan: actionable checklist i hear:
- runtime: ensure header/param pin overrides default (sidd)
- runtime: emit `x-redwood-model*` headers (tilly)
- sdk: add `pinModel` helper + docs + examples (lucas)
- qa: add eval gates for rollout (qa-bot)
- comms: 2-week notice + console banners + changelog + migration guide (natalie)

any objections? if none i'll open the PRs and the comms draft today.

ada: no objections from infra side. small note: make sure fallback behavior is deterministic — if a pinned model isn't available we should return 503 + structured error rather than silently falling back.

sidd: important — implement a `model-fallback` policy flag per account (enum: fail|fallback-to-compatible|fallback-to-cheapest) so customers can opt-in to graceful fallback, with default = fail. document clearly.

lucas: +1 on model-fallback flag. SDK should expose it as config: `{ fallback: 'fail' }`. also add telemetry event when fallback happens.

morgan: ok adding `model-fallback` to runbook. i'll include sample header usage in the comms:

```
POST /v1/generate
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer <token>
  Model: gpt-redwood-1   # optional, pins model for this request

Response headers:
  x-redwood-model: gpt-redwood-2
  x-redwood-model-origin: default
```

will draft PRs for runtime + SDK + docs. tagging folks: @ada @sidd @tilly @lucas for follow-ups.

natalie: i'll draft the external comms after PRs are merged. plan: internal announcement tomorrow, external notices 14 days before flip.

tilly: tiny UX ask: console should show per-request model in logs and a filter to search by `x-redwood-model`. helps customers debug multi-variant traffic.

qa-bot: once PRs are up, i'll run canary evals automatically and post results in this thread.

morgan: perfect — thanks everyone. i'll post PR links and comms draft here shortly. :thumbsup:

lucas: thanks — i'll start the SDK PR (pin helper + fallback config) today.

ada: noting: do not perform any silent model mapping (e.g., aliasing gpt-redwood-1 -> gpt-redwood-2) without explicit deprecation header. otherwise customers see surprises.

morgan: agreed. we'll add an explicit `Deprecation` response header if/when we start mapping aliases.

(thumbs +1s)
